page.title: Dashboard Overview
page.description: Your command center showing system health, active workflows, and agent status at a glance.

active_workflows.text: Workflows currently executing or queued. High number indicates busy system.

total_agents.text: All agents created in your system. Active agents can execute tasks immediately.

documents_indexed.text: Documents in knowledge base. Searchable by all agents via RAG and semantic search.

system_status.text: Overall platform health. Green = all systems operational. Check component status for details.

create_agent.text: Open agent creation wizard. Fastest way to create a new specialized AI agent.

create_workflow.text: Start new workflow. Pre-filled with defaults for quick execution.

upload_document.text: Add document to knowledge base. Drag-drop or browse files.

page.title: Agent Management
page.description: Create, configure, and monitor AI agents. Each agent is a specialized AI entity with skills, tools, and performance tracking.

total_agents.text: Total number of agents you've created. Each agent is a specialized AI entity with its own model, skills, and tools.

active_agents.text: Agents currently ready to execute tasks. Inactive agents need to be started manually.

agent_types.text: Different agent specializations (Code Architect, Security Expert, etc.). Templates with pre-configured skills.

avg_performance.text: Average success rate across all agents based on task completion quality. Target: >90%

search.text: Search agents by name, type, or description. Filters list in real-time.

status_filter.text: Filter agents by their current status (Active, Idle, Learning, etc.)

type_filter.text: Filter by agent specialization (Code Architect, Security Expert, etc.)

create_button.text: Open 4-step agent creation wizard. Choose template, configure model, assign skills and tools.

all_skills.text: Complete library of available skills. Add these to agents to enhance their capabilities.

agent_skills.text: View and manage skills for a specific agent. Add or remove skills to customize agent expertise.

categories.text: Skills organized by domain (Development, Security, Data, etc.). Browse to find relevant capabilities.

proficiency.text: Skill expertise level calculated from historical performance. More stars = better performance with this skill.

agent_selector.text: Choose an agent to view and modify its configuration

edit_button.text: Opens detailed configuration modal with 5 tabs for fine-tuning agent behavior

template_selection.text: Choose a template or start from scratch. Templates come pre-configured with recommended skills and settings.

name.text: Give your agent a descriptive name. Examples: 'Python Security Reviewer', 'API Documentation Expert'

priority.text: When multiple agents need resources, higher priority agents execute first. High = Critical, Medium = Standard, Low = Background

max_concurrent.text: Maximum tasks this agent can handle simultaneously. Higher = more parallel execution. Range: 1-10, Recommended: 3-5

auto_start.text: Automatically activate this agent when platform starts. Recommended for critical agents.

model_selection.text: Select the LLM that powers this agent. GPT-4 Turbo recommended for code, Claude 3 Opus for analysis. See model comparison for guidance.

temperature.text: Controls randomness. Lower (0.0-0.5) = focused/consistent. Higher (0.7-2.0) = creative/varied. Recommended: 0.7 for most tasks.

max_tokens.text: Maximum length of agent responses. Higher = longer responses but more expensive. Range: 100-4096. Recommended: 2000-3000.

fallback_model.text: Backup model used if primary model fails or hits rate limits. Ensures reliability. Common: GPT-3.5 Turbo as fallback for GPT-4.

skills.text: Choose expertise areas for this agent. Skills enhance prompts with domain knowledge. Recommended: 3-7 skills per agent.

tools.text: External integrations this agent can use (GitHub, Slack, databases, etc.). 400+ tools available via MCP protocol.

page.title: Workflow Management
page.description: Orchestrate complex automation with intelligent multi-agent workflows

active_workflows.text: Workflows currently executing. Includes running and queued workflows.

completed_today.text: Successfully completed workflows in the last 24 hours

avg_duration.text: Average time from start to completion. Helps estimate new workflows.

agent_utilization.text: Percentage of agents currently working on workflows. Higher = busier system. Optimal: 60-80%

progress_bar.text: Visual progress through workflow stages. Each segment represents a task or agent. Percentage shows overall completion.

templates.text: Pre-built workflow templates for common automation patterns. One-click creation with your custom settings.

goal.text: The high-level objective. The orchestrator uses this to decompose tasks. Be specific and clear about desired outcome.

auto_select.text: Let the orchestrator choose optimal agents based on skills and availability. Uses LLM reasoning for intelligent selection.

execution_mode.text: Parallel = run independent tasks simultaneously (faster). Sequential = one at a time (safer). Optimized = smart mix (recommended).

error_handling.text: Stop on Error = halt if any task fails. Continue = skip failed tasks. Retry = auto-retry failures 1-5 times.

phase_decomposition.text: LLM analyzes the goal and breaks it into subtasks with dependencies and priorities.

phase_selection.text: Optimal agents chosen using 4D matching (skills, availability, history, tools). LLM provides reasoning for selections.

phase_context.text: Building optimal prompts for each agent using RAG and memory retrieval. Applies MMR and knapsack optimization.

phase_execution.text: Agents executing their assigned tasks. Progress updates in real-time. Tools called as needed.

page.title: Knowledge Base & Documents
page.description: Manage your organization's knowledge - documents, code, and multimodal content

total_documents.text: Total number of documents uploaded and processed in your knowledge base

processed.text: Documents fully processed and searchable. Processing includes text extraction, chunking, and embedding generation.

processing.text: Documents currently being processed. Typically takes 30-60 seconds per document.

failed.text: Documents that failed processing. Click to see errors and retry. Common causes: unsupported format, corrupted file.

search.text: Search documents by filename, content, or tags. Real-time filtering as you type.

category_filter.text: Filter by document category (auto-detected or manually assigned). Helps organize large document libraries.

semantic_mode.text: Finds conceptually similar content even with different words. Best for understanding-based search. Uses AI embeddings.

keyword_mode.text: Traditional exact-match search. Fast but less intelligent. Good for finding specific terms.

similarity_score.text: Relevance of result to your query. 90-100% = excellent, 70-89% = good, 50-69% = moderate, <50% = weak match

drag_drop.text: Easiest upload method. Drag multiple files at once for batch upload. Supports PDF, Word, Markdown, code files, and more.

supported_formats.text: Supported: PDF, DOCX, MD, TXT, code files (.py, .js, .ts, etc.), CSV, JSON. Max size: 50MB per file.

queue_status.text: Documents waiting to be processed. FIFO order unless priority set. Monitor active processing and completion.

extraction.text: Extracting text from PDF/Word. Also extracts tables, images, and formulas for multimodal support.

chunking.text: Splitting text into searchable chunks. Overlap ensures context preservation. Default: 512 tokens with 50 token overlap.

embedding.text: Creating vector embeddings for semantic search. Uses AI model to convert text to numbers.

indexing.text: Storing in PostgreSQL with pgvector. Makes content searchable via similarity queries.

projects_indexed.text: Code repositories indexed and searchable. Each project is a separate codebase.

files_analyzed.text: Total code files across all projects. Includes classes, functions, and relationships.

relationships.text: Code relationships mapped (imports, calls, dependencies). Enables dependency graphs and call tracing.

page.title: Context Engineering
page.description: Optimize AI performance through intelligent context management and RAG

context_queries.text: Total number of context/RAG queries executed. Higher = more agent activity and knowledge base usage.

retrieval_success.text: Percentage of queries that returned relevant results. Target: >90%. Low rate indicates missing content.

avg_response_time.text: Average time to retrieve and optimize context. Lower = faster agent execution. Target: <1000ms

vector_embeddings.text: Total embeddings in vector database. Each chunk has an embedding for semantic search. Higher = more searchable content.

confidence_score.text: Result confidence: >85% = high (excellent results), 60-85% = medium (good), <60% = low (poor results, refine query)

latency.text: Query response time. Breakdown shows which stage is slow (embedding, search, optimization). Target: <1 second total.

rag_config.text: RAG configs control how documents are retrieved and optimized. Different strategies for different use cases (precision, recall, speed).

retrieval_method.text: Algorithm for finding relevant documents. Cosine similarity (default, fast), Re-ranking (slower, higher quality).

top_k.text: Number of chunks to retrieve before optimization. More = better coverage but slower. Recommended: 5-10

recommendations.text: AI-powered suggestions based on your actual usage patterns. Apply to improve performance, reduce costs, or increase quality.

max_chunks.text: Maximum number of document chunks to retrieve. More = more context but higher cost. Range: 1-20, Default: 5

max_tokens.text: Token budget for context. System optimizes to stay within this limit. Range: 500-8000, Default: 2000

diversity_lambda.text: Balance between relevance and diversity. λ=1 is pure relevance, λ=0 is pure diversity. Recommended: 0.7 (balanced)

search.text: Vector similarity search in database. Finds top 50 candidates based on query embedding.

diversity.text: Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) optimization. Balances similarity and diversity to avoid redundant results.

budget.text: Knapsack optimization. Maximizes information value within token limit. Ensures staying under budget.

format.text: Assembling final context with structure and formatting for LLM consumption.

information_density.text: Percentage of tokens that are relevant to query. Higher = better. Target: >0.75. Excellent: >0.85

page.title: Tools Management
page.description: Browse, configure, and assign MCP tools to agents

available_tools.text: Total tools in registry. 400+ integrations available across 12 categories.

active_assignments.text: Tool-agent connections currently active. Shows how many integrations are being used.

usage_this_week.text: Tool calls made by agents this week. Higher = more integration activity.

developer.text: Developer tools: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Jira. For code management and project tracking.

communication.text: Communication tools: Slack, Discord, Email, Teams. For notifications and messaging.

cloud.text: Cloud services: AWS, Azure, GCP, DigitalOcean. For infrastructure management.

database.text: Database tools: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis. For data operations.

permissions.text: Control what operations agent can perform. Read = query, Write = modify, Execute = admin actions. Use least privilege principle.

credential.text: Which credential to use for authentication. Must be configured in Settings → Credentials first.

page.title: Settings & Configuration
page.description: Configure platform settings, manage credentials, and review security audit logs

name.text: Descriptive name for this credential. Examples: 'Production OpenAI', 'Dev Database', 'Slack Engineering'

environment.text: Separate credentials by environment for safety. Use different credentials for Production vs Development.

test_connection.text: Verify credential works before saving. Highly recommended to catch issues early!

types.text: Pre-configured credential schemas for every major service. Don't create from scratch - use these templates!

audit.text: Every credential access logged for compliance and security. SOC2, GDPR compliant audit trail.

provider.text: LLM provider for orchestrator reasoning. Separate from agent models. Used for task decomposition and agent selection.

temperature.text: Orchestrator creativity. Lower = more consistent decomposition. Recommended: 0.3 for deterministic behavior.

llm_driven.text: Orchestrator uses reasoning to select agents. Higher quality but slower. Disable for algorithmic fallback.

max_file_size.text: Maximum file size to index (larger files skipped). Prevents indexing huge binary files. Recommended: 1MB

exclude_patterns.text: Glob patterns to skip during indexing. Standard: node_modules, __pycache__, venv, .git

auto_reindex.text: Automatically re-index on code changes (via webhooks). Enable for active projects, disable for archived.

api_limit.text: Maximum API calls per minute (all users combined). Protects against overload. Default: 1,000 req/min

workflow_limit.text: Maximum workflows created per hour. Prevents runaway automation. Default: 100/hour

llm_limit.text: Limit to stay within provider tier limits and control costs. Based on your OpenAI/Anthropic tier.

page.title: Performance Analytics
page.description: Data-driven insights into platform performance and optimization opportunities

success_rate.text: Percentage of successful executions. Target: >90%. Green = >90%, Yellow = 80-90%, Red = <80%

quality_score.text: Average quality rating of outputs. Range: 0.0-1.0. Target: >0.85. Based on multiple quality dimensions.

response_time.text: Average time from task start to completion. Target: <5 seconds for most tasks.

utilization.text: How busy are agents? 60-80% is optimal - agents working but not overloaded. <40% = underutilized, >90% = need more agents

efficiency.text: Combined metric: (Success Rate × Quality Score) / (Avg Time × Avg Cost). Stars: ⭐ (Poor) to ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (Excellent)

total_spend.text: Total platform spend across all LLM providers. Includes OpenAI, Anthropic, and embeddings.

optimization.text: AI-powered cost optimization suggestions. Click 'Apply' to auto-apply safe optimizations.

input.text: Type your question or message. Press Enter to send, Shift+Enter for new line. Ask naturally!

code_references.text: Code snippets from your indexed repositories. Click to see full file or copy code.

document_references.text: Documents referenced in response. Click to view full document or specific page.

page.title: Playbooks
page.description: Automatically discovered patterns from successful workflows. Reuse proven strategies with 1-click.

confidence.text: Statistical confidence in discovered pattern. Higher = more reliable. Based on consistency across multiple executions.

support.text: How many workflows match this pattern. Higher = more common pattern. Minimum: 5 for discovery.

mine_patterns.text: Analyze workflow history to discover new patterns. Uses FP-Growth algorithm. Runs automatically nightly or on-demand.

create_workflow.text: Create workflow from this playbook. Pre-configured with proven agent selections, tools, and settings.

time_range.text: Filter by date range to narrow results. Options: Last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, or custom range.

search.text: Search by name, description, or tags. Case-insensitive, real-time filtering.

refresh.text: Reload data from server. Use if data seems stale. Most pages auto-refresh every 30-60 seconds.

export.text: Export data to CSV, JSON, or PDF for external analysis or reporting.

close.text: Close this modal. Press Esc key or click outside to close. Changes not saved unless you clicked Save.
